items.title: Exhale Emphasis
items.description: Long exhales activate your parasympathetic nervous system: the 'rest and digest' mode that counters stress.

items.title: Optimal Rate
items.description: Breathing at 5-6 breaths per minute maximizes heart rate variability (HRV), your body's stress resilience marker.

items.title: Attention Anchor
items.description: Counting breath phases interrupts rumination and catastrophic thinking: you can't panic and count simultaneously.

comfortTips.title: Comfort Tips
items: Find a quiet spot when possible, even 30 seconds alone helps
Don't force deep breaths, smaller, smoother breaths work better
Start with just 1 minute. That's often enough
Skip breath holds if they feel uncomfortable
If you feel dizzy or tingly, return to normal breathing

items.question: I only have 30 seconds. Will this help?

parts.text: Yes. The physiological sigh (double inhale + long exhale) works in just 1-3 breaths. It's specifically designed for acute stress relief when you can't step away.

items.question: Can I do this at the dinner table without looking weird?

parts.text: can be disguised as a natural tired sigh, people sigh all the time. For longer techniques, excuse yourself briefly.

items.question: What if I'm too stressed to focus on breathing?

parts.text: Use the visual guide on your phone, watching the animation is easier than counting. Start with just one physiological sigh to take the edge off.

items.question: Which technique is best for holiday stress?

parts.text: Physiological sigh for acute moments (rising tension, panic). Coherent breathing for sustained calm (travel, long gatherings). 4-7-8 for bedtime after exhausting days.

items.question: How is this different from just 'taking deep breaths'?

parts.text: Random deep breaths often make anxiety worse by over-breathing. These techniques use specific rhythms that activate your parasympathetic nervous system.

items.question: Will this help with holiday travel anxiety too?

parts.text: Yes. Coherent breathing creates sustained calm that lasts for hours. See our travel anxiety guide for the complete protocol.

items.title: Panic Attacks
items.description: Stop panic fast with physiological sigh

footer: Stop if dizzy, tingly, or chest-tight. These are self-regulation tools, not medical treatment. If you have ongoing mental health concerns, please consult a professional.

schema.howToName: How to Calm Holiday Stress with Breathing
schema.howToDescription: Use the physiological sigh technique to quickly calm holiday stress in 30 seconds.

howToSteps.name: Notice the stress
howToSteps.text: Recognize when you're tensing up: clenching jaw, tight shoulders, racing thoughts, or the urge to snap.

howToSteps.name: First inhale
howToSteps.text: Breathe in deeply through your nose, filling your lungs about 80-90%. Let your belly expand.

howToSteps.name: Second inhale (top-up)
howToSteps.text: Without exhaling, take a second, shorter sniff through your nose to fully inflate your lungs.

howToSteps.name: Long exhale
howToSteps.text: Exhale slowly and completely through your mouth, making the exhale longer than both inhales combined.

howToSteps.name: Repeat if needed
howToSteps.text: One sigh often provides immediate relief. Do 2-3 if you need a full reset.
